content.text:
Zero tests currently touch `PullRequestPanel` or any "GitHub CLI …" string — the warning UI is entirely uncovered, and we're adding a third case to it. `ghPreflight:496` already checks `timedOut` first, so `signaled` slots in cleanly after it.

**Coverage diagram (post-decision scope):**

```
CODE PATHS                                                    USER FLOWS
[~] Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift                            [+] The reported bug
  └── CommandResult.signaled  (new)                             ├── [GAP] switch workrooms mid-probe → no false warning
      ├── [GAP] cancelled → signaled=T, exit 9                  └── [GAP] ⌘Tab away/back ×2 → no false warning
      ├── [GAP] TIMEOUT → timedOut=T *AND* signaled=T          [+] Genuine auth states
      │        ^^ TRAP: terminate() is SIGTERM, so every         ├── [GAP] real logout → warns on FIRST probe
      │           consumer must test timedOut BEFORE signaled    ├── [GAP] re-auth → clears within 10s (neg. TTL)
      ├── [GAP] clean exit → signaled=F                         └── [GAP] [→E2E] old gh → "too old", not "not signed in"
      └── [★★ TESTED] launch fail → 127 — SCRTests:testLaunch* [+] Interrupted writes
[~] Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift                           └── [GAP] sleep/wake during push → no "git exited 15"
  ├── classifyGitHubCLI
  │   ├── [★★★ TESTED] 127 / timeout / success / 401 /
  │   │                {"hosts":{}} / non-JSON — :672-800
  │   ├── [GAP] signaled + empty stdout    → .available
  │   ├── [GAP] signaled + truncated JSON  → .available
  │   ├── [GAP] signaled + COMPLETE 401    → .notAuthenticated   ← ordering lock
  │   └── [GAP] unknown-flag shape         → .tooOld
  └── ghPreflight
      └── [GAP] signaled → .keepPrior (and timedOut still wins)
[~] Core/AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift
  └── refreshGitHubCLI
      ├── [GAP] cancelled → status AND stamp untouched          ← CRITICAL REGRESSION (iron rule)
      └── [GAP] force bypasses TTL
[+] Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift  (new actor, from D4)
      ├── [GAP] two concurrent callers → exactly ONE `gh auth` invocation
      ├── [GAP] inside TTL → no re-probe
      ├── [GAP] .notAuthenticated 12s old → re-probes;  .available 12s old → does not
      └── [GAP] reset() isolation (process-wide, same rule as VCSToolVersionCache)
[~] Core/VCSWriting.swift
      └── [GAP] classify + classifyCommit: signaled → interrupted, not "exited 9"
[~] Views/PullRequestPanel.swift
      └── [GAP] ghWarning copy: 4 states, incl. no install link on .tooOld

COVERAGE: 6/29 paths (21%)  |  Code: 6/23 (26%)  |  User flows: 0/6 (0%)
QUALITY: ★★★:1 cluster ★★:1  |  GAPS: 23 (1 E2E)  |  1 CRITICAL regression test (mandatory, no question)
```

The regression test is mandatory under the iron rule. One real decision on the UI layer:

questions.question:
D8 — Issue 6 [P2] (confidence: 10/10) — The gh-warning UI has ZERO test coverage and we're adding a third state to it. `PullRequestPanel.swift:31-54`, `UITestFixture.swift` (no gh seam) <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-test-ghwarning-coverage>

ELI10: `ghWarning` decides three things from one enum — the title, the body, and whether to show the "Install gh…" link — using a chain of `status == .notInstalled` ternaries at `:36`, `:42-44`, `:48`. I grepped: no test in `WorkroomAppTests` or `WorkroomAppUITests` references `PullRequestPanel`, `ghWarning`, or any "GitHub CLI …" string. Adding `.tooOld` converts those ternaries into a switch, which is exactly the edit where a case gets mapped to the wrong copy — and the failure mode is silent, because a wrong-but-plausible warning still renders fine. There is also no gh seam in `UITestFixture`, and `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode (`:104`), so an XCUITest cannot currently drive any gh state at all.

Stakes if we pick wrong: the whole point of this PR is that Workroom stops telling you something false about your auth. Shipping a new warning state whose copy nothing verifies means the next refactor can silently reintroduce a wrong message — the same class of bug, one layer up.

Recommendation: C — extract the copy into a pure function and unit-test all four states (that is where the regression actually lives and it is nearly free), AND add the fixture seam plus XCUITests, because you have asked for XCUITest coverage on new macapp UI before and the fixture gap will otherwise block every future gh-state UI test too.

Completeness: A=7/10, B=8/10, C=10/10, D=3/10

Pros / cons:

options.label: Both: pure copy function + fixture seam & XCUITests (recommended)
options.description:
Extract `ghWarningCopy(for:) -> (title, body, showsInstallLink)` and unit-test all four states, AND add a `ghStatus` fixture flag that seeds the status at launch so XCUITests can assert each rendered warning. (human: ~4h / CC: ~30min)

✅ Covers both layers: the mapping logic where a switch edit actually breaks, and the render path proving the panel really shows it.
✅ Builds the fixture seam once, unblocking every future gh-state UI test instead of leaving the gap for the next feature.
✅ Matches your standing preference for XCUITest coverage on new macapp UI, not just unit tests.
❌ Most expensive option, and the fixture flag has to be honoured around the `:104` early-return without letting a real probe overwrite the seeded value.

options.label: Pure copy function + unit tests only
options.description:
Extract the copy mapping out of the view body and assert all four states in `WorkroomAppTests`. No fixture changes, no XCUITest.

✅ Pins the exact regression risk — a case mapped to the wrong title, body, or link — in a fast test with no UI harness.
✅ Also improves the view: the body loses a three-ternary chain and reads as a single switch.
❌ Does not prove the panel actually renders the copy, so a broken gate at `:17` would still ship green.
❌ Leaves the `UITestFixture` gh gap in place for the next person who needs it.

options.label: XCUITest + fixture seam only
options.description:
Add the `ghStatus` fixture flag and assert the rendered warning text for each state through the UI test scheme, leaving the view code as-is.

✅ Tests what the user actually sees, end to end through the real view hierarchy and the real gate at `:17`.
✅ Adds the reusable fixture seam that is currently missing entirely.
❌ Slow feedback for what is fundamentally a string-mapping bug, and per your own note UI tests must be scoped to single test methods to stay usable.
❌ Leaves the ternary chain in the view body, so the mapping has no cheap unit-level guard.

options.label: Classifier tests only, no UI test
options.description:
Accept the UI as untested: assert that `classifyGitHubCLI` returns `.tooOld` and trust the panel switch by inspection.

✅ Smallest test surface, and the classifier is where the measured behaviour actually lives.
✅ No new fixture machinery and no UI-test runtime added to the suite.
❌ Ships a user-facing warning string with nothing verifying it — the precise thing this PR exists to stop getting wrong.
❌ A mis-mapped switch case is invisible to every test in the suite.

cat > "$OUT" <<'EOF'
# Test Plan
Generated by /plan-eng-review on 2026-08-05
Branch: master
Repo: joelmoss/workroom (macOS app, macapp/)

## Affected Surfaces
- Changes inspector -> Pull Request section (`PullRequestPanel`) — the gh warning block: title, body,
  and the conditional "Install gh…" link. Four states must each render correct copy:
  available (no warning), notInstalled, notAuthenticated, tooOld (new).
- Changes inspector -> PR number badge and PR actions menu (`ChangesPanel:220,240`) — gated on
  `githubCLIStatus == .available`; must stay hidden for tooOld.
- VCS toolbar failure sheet — an interrupted push/pull/commit must not print "git exited 15".

## Key Interactions to Verify
- Arrow-key / click through several workrooms within ~1 second while a status sweep is running.
  Expected: the PR panel never shows "GitHub CLI not signed in" while `gh auth status` really succeeds.
- ⌘Tab away from and back to the app twice in quick succession (triggers reloadIfStale -> a second
  sweep that cancels the first mid-probe). Same expectation.
- Manual Refresh button in the Changes section header (the only force:true path).
- Open two app windows at once: exactly one `gh auth status` should run, not one per window.
- Sleep/wake (or an OS SIGTERM) during a `git push` from the VCS toolbar.

## Edge Cases
- Genuinely signed out: warning must still appear on the FIRST probe, not after a delay.
- Re-authenticate while the app is open: the warning must clear within ~10s (negative TTL).
- gh older than 2.57 (rejects `--json`): must read "GitHub CLI too old" with an upgrade instruction,
  never "not signed in", and must show no "Install gh…" link.
- gh present but network unreachable (transport error, non-401): must NOT warn.
- Token rejected (HTTP 401 / Bad credentials): must warn.
- `gh` removed from PATH entirely: "GitHub CLI not found" with the install link.

## Critical Paths
- Cancelled probe must leave BOTH `githubCLIStatus` and its TTL stamp untouched. This is the reported
  bug: the poisoned write stamped its own TTL and thereby suppressed every repair for 60s.
- A timed-out child sets timedOut AND signaled (SIGTERM), so every consumer must test timedOut first.
- A signalled child that nevertheless emitted a complete 401 verdict must still be believed.
EOF

content.text:
Section 4 — Performance. Evaluated, no action items:

- **Probe count goes down, not up.** The D4 single-flight actor collapses N-windows-at-launch into one `gh auth status`. The `.tooOld` detection reads the *existing* invocation's stderr, so it adds zero processes. `signaled` is one Bool on a struct.
- **One real consequence of D4 worth naming:** modelling the actor on `VCSToolVersionCache` means the probe lives in an unstructured `Task`, so a cancelled lane no longer SIGKILLs the `gh` child — it runs to completion (≤10s `ciTimeout`). That is *more* child lifetime than today, and it is the correct trade: the probe now produces a real verdict instead of a killed one. Same behaviour `VCSToolVersionCache` already ships.
- **Negative TTL cost, bounded.** A rejected-token user re-probes at most every 10s per user-driven lane invocation, each a network round trip. Logged-out-with-no-token returns instantly (measured). Flat 10s rather than backoff matches `applyCIStatus:567-568`, which already records "true exponential backoff is a future refinement" — same call, same reason.
- No database, no N+1, no memory concern. XCUITests add suite time; scope them with `-only-testing:` per your existing rule.

Now the outside voice (Codex is authenticated).

THE PLAN:

# Fix the false, sticky "GitHub CLI not signed in" in the PR panel (workroom macOS app, macapp/)

## Reported symptom
The PR panel intermittently claims `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then recovers on its own about a minute later.

## Root cause (measured, not inferred)
A superseded status sweep (`macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:60` `statusSweepTask?.cancel()`) or a workroom switched mid-probe (`:118` `selectionStatusTask?.cancel()`) cancels the task awaiting `gh auth status --active --json hosts`. The runner's `onCancel` SIGKILLs the child (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:301-307`), but its `withCheckedContinuation` is NON-throwing, so `terminationHandler` (`:252-268`) still resumes with `exitCode: 9` (SIGKILL, measured), `timedOut: false`, and empty-or-half-written stdout.

That walks `WorkroomStatusResolver.classifyGitHubCLI` (`:434-444`): not 127, not timed out, no parseable JSON, so it falls to `return r.ok ? .available : .notAuthenticated` and yields `.notAuthenticated`.

`refreshGitHubCLI` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:103-113`) then writes that verdict AND stamps `ghStatusCheckedAt` with no `Task.isCancelled` check — the only mutation in that file buried behind an await, so the callers' guards at `:86`/`:144` come too late. The stamp is what makes it sticky: the TTL gate at `:105-109` early-returns for every unforced caller, so for 60s every lane that would have healed the value is suppressed by the value's own stamp, and `:87`/`:145` gate off the whole CI/PR probe. Only the manual Refresh button (`ChangesPanel.swift:143`, the sole force:true path) escapes early. The verdict lives on the process-wide `ProjectStore.shared.githubCLIStatus`, so one window's cancelled probe paints and suppresses every other window's panel.

Measured against real gh 2.97.0: the `--json` payload goes to stdout and exit is 0 in all three genuine states (signed in `state:"success"`; bad token `state:"error"` + `HTTP 401 ... Bad credentials`; no config `{"hosts":{}}`). So the exit-code fallback is never reached in normal operation — everything landing there is ambiguous by construction. A keyring/transport failure produces a POPULATED host entry with a non-401 error, already routed to `.available` by `isGitHubAuthFailure` (`:479-482`).

## Approved changes (each was an interactive decision)

1. Cancellation guard: `if Task.isCancelled { return }` in `refreshGitHubCLI` between the await and BOTH the value write and the stamp.

2. `CommandResult.signaled` (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:8-20`): new field set from `finished.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal` in `terminationHandler`. Explicit init with `signaled: Bool = false` last (a `let x = false` property is EXCLUDED from the synthesized memberwise init, so a defaulted `let` would silently break). ~63 `CommandResult(` sites all use labelled args, so a trailing defaulted param keeps them compiling. Precedent: `WorkroomCLI.swift:35-44` already carries this exact field with this exact rationale, shipped as commit a64e4269 "stop 'exited with code 15' dialog on wake from sleep".

3. `classifyGitHubCLI` consumes `signaled` AFTER the JSON parse, not beside `timedOut`: a signalled child that nevertheless emitted a complete 401 verdict has genuinely told us the token is bad. `ghPreflight` (`:495-504`) gets `if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }` after its `timedOut` check.

4. New `GitHubCLIStatus.tooOld`: gh < 2.57 REJECTS `--json` (measured: exit 1, empty stdout, stderr `unknown flag: --json`), so a signed-in user on old gh currently reads as permanently logged out. Detect that shape and render an upgrade instruction. `PullRequestPanel.swift:36,42-44,48` ternaries become a switch; its copy is extracted to a pure `ghWarningCopy(for:) -> (title, body, showsInstallLink)`. Rejected alternative: re-running plain `gh auth status` (two classifiers to keep in sync — the code warns about exactly that drift at `:485-488` — and it reinstates the issue-#86 network-blip flap).

5. Asymmetric TTL: `.notAuthenticated` is trusted for 10s, everything else for the existing 60s. It is both the alarming answer and the sink every ambiguous result falls into, and it gates the whole PR/CI lane. A genuine logout still warns on the FIRST probe; only caching shortens.

6. Single-flight actor for the gh auth verdict, modelled on `VCSToolVersionCache` (`VCSToolVersions.swift:183-206`), which solves the identical problem for tool versions ("a fact about the machine, not about a window"). Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, and `AppStore` is per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, so two windows both probe and last-write-wins. The actor owns the TTL and the in-flight probe; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` stays as the SwiftUI-observable mirror. Needs `reset()` for test isolation.

7. `VCSWriting.swift:1099` and `:1197` consume `signaled`: today a signalled `git push` with empty stderr renders the literal string `git exited 15` in the VCS failure sheet — verbatim the dialog commit a64e4269 claims to have stopped, because that fix never reached `StatusCommandRunner`. Map to `.other("<tool> was interrupted")`; `.other` already carries Retry as its recovery, so no new enum case.

8. `UITestFixture` gains a `ghStatus` seam (currently there is none, and `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode at `:104`) so XCUITests can drive each warning state.

9. Prose corrections: the comment at `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:440-442` claims the fallback covers "pre-2.57 gh without --json" — false, old gh rejects the flag. And `TODOS.md:202-207` defers a related `withTimeout` cancellation fix on the grounds that "every call site already checks Task.isCancelled before merging a stale result, so state stays correct" — this bug is the counterexample; the rationale gets corrected while the deferral stands.

## Tests planned
- `StatusCommandRunnerTests` (extend the existing real-process cancellation test at `:49-78`): cancelled => signaled true, exitCode 9, timedOut false. Also: a TIMEOUT sets timedOut AND signaled (terminate() is SIGTERM), so every consumer must test timedOut first. Clean exit => signaled false. Launch failure stays 127 with signaled false.
- `WorkroomStatusResolverTests` (style at `:672-800`): signaled+empty => .available; signaled+truncated JSON => .available; signaled+COMPLETE 401 => .notAuthenticated (ordering lock); unknown-flag shape => .tooOld; ghPreflight signaled => .keepPrior.
- `WorkroomStatusTests`: CRITICAL regression — a cancelled `refreshGitHubCLI` leaves both `githubCLIStatus` and `ghStatusCheckedAt` untouched. Driven by a gated double that blocks inside the gh probe until cancelled and then RETURNS the SIGKILL shape rather than throwing (the runner's continuation is non-throwing).
- New actor tests: two concurrent callers => exactly ONE gh invocation; inside TTL => no re-probe; `.notAuthenticated` 12s old => re-probes; `.available` 12s old => does not; force bypasses TTL; reset() isolation.
- `VCSWriting` tests: signaled => interrupted, timedOut still => .timedOut(action).
- Unit tests for all four `ghWarningCopy` states; XCUITests per state via the new fixture seam.

## Verification
`make app-test` (read pass/fail from the .xcresult via xcresulttool), `make app-lint`, `make app-format`. Manual repro before and after: switch workrooms rapidly, and ⌘Tab away/back twice while a sweep runs. Genuine-logout check under a throwaway GH_CONFIG_DIR/$HOME.

    let projectRoot: String

/// distinctions the status UI's unknown/stale/absent matrix depends on.

  let stdout: String
  let stderr: String
  let exitCode: Int32
  let timedOut: Bool

  /// `/usr/bin/env` exits 127 when the command (git/jj/gh) isn't on PATH.
  static let commandNotFound: Int32 = 127
  /// git exits 128 for "not a git repository" and similar fatal usage errors.
  static let gitFatal: Int32 = 128

codex
1. The plan has two owners for TTL state. The actor “owns the TTL,” yet the regression test still requires `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` to remain untouched. Keeping both creates divergent truth; removing the timestamp invalidates the test and existing proxies in [AppStore.swift](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:294).

2. The single-flight cancellation model is undefined. Copying `VCSToolVersionCache` means its unstructured `Task` outlives a cancelled waiter, so the planned SIGKILL-shaped regression double will never exercise the real path. If the probe instead inherits caller cancellation, the actor may cache the ambiguous result even though `AppStore` refuses to mirror it.

3. `signaled + malformed output => .available` is still lying. It merely replaces a false negative with a false positive and can erase a legitimate `.notAuthenticated`, `.notInstalled`, or `.tooOld` state. Cancellation and signals mean “keep prior,” not “available.” The planned tests explicitly lock in the wrong behavior.

4. Old-gh detection targets the wrong compatibility boundary. The repository says the 2.57 floor exists because `--active` landed then ([macapp/README.md](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/README.md:19)), but the plan only detects `unknown flag: --json`. Versions supporting JSON but predating `--active` will still be reported as logged out.

5. A static shared actor breaks the test-isolation guarantee documented by `AppStore()`: fresh `ProjectStore`s currently do not pollute one another ([AppStore.swift](/Users/joelmoss/dev/workroom/macapp/WorkroomApp/Core/AppStore.swift:793)). `reset()` is insufficient and race-prone: an old in-flight task can finish after reset and repopulate the cache. Parallel tests can also consume another test’s injected runner. The cache should be injected or owned by `ProjectStore`.

6. `force` during an existing non-forced flight is unspecified. Joining it means manual Refresh does not truly force; starting another violates single-flight. This needs an explicit contract and test.

7. TTL tests need an injected clock. Otherwise “12 seconds old” either sleeps for 12 seconds or reaches into actor internals. Using `Date` also permits a backward wall-clock adjustment to extend the cache indefinitely.

8. The fixture seam is incomplete. Since `refreshGitHubCLI` returns immediately in fixture mode, merely adding `UITestFixture.ghStatus` changes nothing. It must be applied during fixture loading and manual reseeding, without being overwritten by the optimistic `.available` default.

9. Most of this is unrelated scope. The reported defect is fixed by the post-await cancellation guard. Old-gh UX, asymmetric caching, global single-flight, VCS write copy, and fixture expansion are separate changes with independent failure modes. Bundling them makes the cancellation fix harder to validate and revert.

D10 — Tension 2 [P1] (confidence: 9/10) — Where does the single-flight cache live, and what are its cancellation / force / clock contracts? `AppStore.swift:296-299`, `:793-795`, `VCSToolVersions.swift:183-206` <gstack-qid:plan-eng-review-tension-actor-ownership>

ELI10: I recommended copying `VCSToolVersionCache`, which is a `static let shared` actor with a tests-only `reset()`. Codex found three problems with that here. First, `AppStore.swift:793-795` documents a real guarantee — "tests build an isolated `AppStore()` (own fresh `ProjectStore`)" — and a static cache punches straight through it; `make app-test` runs PARALLEL, so one test's injected fake runner can serve another test's probe, and `reset()` cannot stop an already-in-flight task from repopulating the cache afterwards. Second, if the cache owns the TTL then `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` (proxied at `AppStore.swift:296-299`) is a second owner of the same truth. Third, three contracts are simply unwritten: does a cancelled waiter kill the probe, does `force` join an in-flight non-forced probe or start a new one, and how does a test age a timestamp without sleeping.

One consequence worth seeing clearly: if the probe runs in a task the cache owns rather than the caller's, a cancelled lane no longer kills the `gh` child — so for this path the SIGKILL-shaped result stops occurring at all. The cancellation guard and `signaled` still earn their place (OS kills, crashes, sleep/wake, and every other `CommandResult` consumer), but the regression test must then be written against the store write, not against a fabricated SIGKILL from the actor.

Stakes if we pick wrong: a static cache produces flaky parallel tests that look like product bugs, and two TTL owners drift. Unspecified force means your Refresh button silently does not refresh.

Recommendation: A — instance-owned gets isolation for free from a guarantee the codebase already documents, kills the second TTL owner, and lets the three contracts be written down and tested rather than inferred.

✅ Test isolation comes free from the existing `AppStore()` guarantee, so no static state, no `reset()`, and no cross-test runner leakage under parallel execution.

Everything else you approved is hardening that rides along: the `.tooOld` state and its panel copy, the instance-owned single-flight cache with three new contracts, the asymmetric TTL, the VCS-write interrupted message, and the fixture seam plus XCUITests. Codex's argument is about revertability: if the combined PR misbehaves in a way you notice next week, reverting it also reverts the fix you actually wanted. Splitting keeps all the approved work — it only changes what lands together.

One real cost of splitting, worth seeing before you choose: the cache becomes the sole TTL owner and DELETES `ghStatusCheckedAt`, but the regression test in a fix-first PR must assert against `ghStatusCheckedAt` because it still exists there. input.content:
# Fix the false, sticky "GitHub CLI not signed in" in the PR panel

## Context

The PR panel intermittently claims `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then recovers on its own about a
minute later. Root cause confirmed by measurement.

A superseded status sweep (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:60`) or a workroom switched mid-probe
(`:118`) cancels the task awaiting `gh auth status --active --json hosts`. The runner's `onCancel`
SIGKILLs the child (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:301-307`), but its `withCheckedContinuation` is
**non-throwing**, so `terminationHandler` (`:252-268`) still resumes with `exitCode: 9` (SIGKILL —
measured; signal numbers stay well below `commandNotFound: 127`), `timedOut: false`, and
empty-or-half-written stdout.

That walks the classifier (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:434-444`): not 127, not timed out, no
parseable JSON, so it falls to `r.ok ? .available : .notAuthenticated` → **`.notAuthenticated`**.

`refreshGitHubCLI` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:103-113`) then writes that verdict **and stamps
`ghStatusCheckedAt`** with no `Task.isCancelled` check. It is the only mutation in that file buried
*behind* an await, so the callers' guards at `:86`/`:144` come too late. The stamp is the sticky
half: the TTL gate at `:105-109` early-returns for every unforced caller, so for 60s every lane that
would have healed the value is suppressed by the value's own stamp, while `:87`/`:145` gate off the
whole CI/PR probe. Only the manual Refresh button (`ChangesPanel.swift:143`, the sole `force: true`
path) escapes early. The verdict lives on the process-wide `ProjectStore.shared.githubCLIStatus`, so
one window's cancelled probe paints and suppresses every other window's panel.

```
  THE POISONED-CACHE LOOP  (what makes a 200ms blip last 60 seconds)

  lane B starts ──cancel()──► lane A's `gh auth status` child
                                      │ SIGKILL
                                      ▼
                        CommandResult(exitCode: 9, timedOut: false, stdout: "")
                                      │
                     classifyGitHubCLI │ not 127 · not timedOut · no JSON
                                      ▼
                             .notAuthenticated          ◄── a lie: nothing was learned
                                      │
                  refreshGitHubCLI:112 │ writes value AND stamps TTL   (no isCancelled guard)
                                      ▼
                 ProjectStore.shared ──┬──► PR panel: "GitHub CLI not signed in"   (every window)
                                       └──► ghStatusCheckedAt = now
                                                     │
                     ┌───────────────────────────────┘
                     ▼
              TTL gate :105-109 ──► every unforced caller returns EARLY for 60s
                     │                    ▲
                     └────────────────────┘  the wrong value suppresses its own repair
                          escape hatch: ONLY the Refresh button (force: true)
```

Measured against real gh 2.97.0: the `--json` payload goes to **stdout** and exit is **0** in all
three genuine states (signed in `state:"success"`; bad token `state:"error"` + `HTTP 401 ... Bad
credentials`; no config `{"hosts":{}}`). So the exit-code fallback is never reached in normal
operation — everything landing there is ambiguous by construction. A keyring/transport failure
produces a *populated* host entry with a non-401 error, already routed away by
`isGitHubAuthFailure` (`:479-482`).

Outcome wanted: an uninformative probe must never publish anything, and an ambiguous one must never
be trusted for a minute.

## What already exists (reuse, don't rebuild)

| Sub-problem | Existing code | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| "child died by signal; exit code is a signal number" | `WorkroomCLI.swift:35-44` `CLIResult.signaled`, consumed `:287`; shipped as `a64e4269` "stop 'exited with code 15' dialog on wake from sleep" | Copy the field and the name onto `CommandResult` |
| "a blip must not overwrite a good value" | `ghPreflight` `.keepPrior` (`:489-504`); `applyCIStatus:564-570` / `applyPRStatus:596-599` don't-stamp-on-first-blip | Adopt `.keepPrior` for the auth probe too |
| cancellation guard idiom | `Task.isCancelled` at `:82`, `:86`, `:96`, `:136`, `:140`, `:144`, `:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`, `:446`, `:493`, `:724` | Same idiom, moved inside `refreshGitHubCLI` |
| "machine fact, one probe for N windows" | `VCSToolVersionCache` actor (`VCSToolVersions.swift:183-206`) — the pattern, but **static**, which is why we deviate | Instance-owned, see PR2 |
| tool floor + warn, don't guess | git ≥ 2.41 / jj ≥ 0.43 floors, `warnings(hasJJProject:)` | `.tooOld` follows the same posture for gh |
| test isolation | `AppStore.swift:793-795` — "tests build an isolated `AppStore()` (own fresh `ProjectStore`)" | Own the cache per `ProjectStore` so this holds for free |
| signalled-probe safety, already correct | `VCSToolVersions.status:148-154` maps a signalled `--version` to `.unknown`, which `warnings:107-108` ignores | No change; verified not affected |

Nothing here is rebuilt. The one genuinely new type is `GitHubAuthCache` (PR2).

---

# PR1 — the fix (small, independently revertable)

## 1. `CommandResult.signaled` — `Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`

- `CommandResult` (`:8-20`) gains `let signaled: Bool` plus an **explicit init** with
  `signaled: Bool = false` last. Do **not** write `let signaled: Bool = false`: Swift drops a
  `let` with an initial value from the synthesized memberwise init entirely, and the only compile
  error is the one line that tries to set it. All ~63 `CommandResult(` sites use labelled args, so a
  trailing defaulted parameter keeps every one compiling; no consumer compares whole values, so the
  widened synthesized `==` breaks nothing.
- `terminationHandler` (`:262-267`): `signaled: finished.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal`.
- **Trap to comment loudly:** the timeout path calls `proc.terminate()` (`:239`) — SIGTERM — so a
  timed-out child has `timedOut == true` **AND** `signaled == true`. Every consumer must therefore
  test `timedOut` first. `markTimedOut()` already precedes `terminate()` at `:237-240`, so the
  ordering is safe as long as classifiers respect it.

## 2. "No news" becomes representable — `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`

`.available` is not "no news", it is a positive claim that gh works — and writing it over a correct
`.notAuthenticated` erases a true warning with a false silence. The codebase already has the right
word two functions down (`ghPreflight`'s `.keepPrior`). So:

```swift
enum GHAuthProbe: Equatable {
  case verdict(GitHubCLIStatus)
  case keepPrior          // the probe told us nothing — killed, crashed, timed out
}

static func classifyGitHubCLI(_ r: CommandResult) -> GHAuthProbe {
  if r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .verdict(.notInstalled) }
  if r.timedOut { return .keepPrior }                                  // MUST precede signaled
  if let s = classifyGitHubCLIJSON(r.stdout) { return .verdict(s) }     // a complete verdict wins
  if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }                                  // no verdict ⇒ no evidence
  return r.ok ? .verdict(.available) : .verdict(.notAuthenticated)
}
```

`resolveGitHubCLI()` returns `GHAuthProbe`. Two orderings are load-bearing and both get a test:
`timedOut` before `signaled` (a timeout is also a signal), and the JSON parse before `signaled` (a
child that emitted a complete 401 and was *then* killed has genuinely told us the token is bad).

This also corrects the pre-existing `.available`-on-timeout lie at `:436`.

`ghPreflight` (`:495-504`) gets `if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }` immediately after its own
`timedOut` check. Not a live bug — all four apply sites (`:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`) are guarded
— so comment it as braces to those guards' belt.

## 3. Nothing from a cancelled or uninformative probe is published — `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`

```swift
let probe = await resolver.resolveGitHubCLI()
if Task.isCancelled { return }                            // a cancelled probe holds no fact
guard case .verdict(let status) = probe else { return }   // .keepPrior: no write, NO STAMP
githubCLIStatus = status
ghStatusCheckedAt = Date()
```

Bail entirely rather than write-value-but-skip-stamp: a cancelled probe's value is garbage too.
Comment why, because the instinct that produced the bug ("a machine-global fact is worth recording
even from a cancelled task") is defensible and wrong.

`.keepPrior` deliberately does **not** stamp, so the next lane re-probes instead of trusting a
non-answer for the full TTL. That is the structural repair; the asymmetric TTL in PR2 is then only
about re-confirming a *real* `.notAuthenticated` sooner.

## 4. `VCSWriting.swift` — stop printing a signal number as an exit code

`:1099` and `:1197` end with `.other("\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)")` when stderr is empty, so a
signalled `git push` renders the literal `git exited 15` in the failure sheet — verbatim the dialog
`a64e4269` claims to have stopped, because that fix never reached this runner. Insert immediately
before each fallback, so any real stderr still classifies:

```swift
let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other("\(tool) was interrupted") }
return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
```

`.other` already carries Retry as its recovery, which is correct for an interrupted write, so no new
enum case. **Rebase note:** `VCSWriting.swift` has uncommitted changes in the working tree.

## 5. Prose corrections (part of the change, not follow-ups)

- `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:440-442` claims the fallback covers "pre-2.57 gh without `--json`".
  Measured false — an old gh *rejects* the flag (exit 1, empty stdout, `unknown flag: --json`).
  Rewrite to say what the fallback actually covers, and point at PR2 for the real handling.
- `TODOS.md:202-207` defers the `withTimeout` cancellation fix on the grounds that "every call site
  already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result … so state stays correct". This bug
  is the counterexample, and the consequence was a wrong published value, not wasted CPU. Correct the
  rationale; **keep the deferral** — that entry's mechanism (`withTimeout`) is genuinely unrelated to
  this one (`runner.run`'s non-throwing continuation).

---

# PR2 — hardening (all approved, lands after PR1)

## 6. `GitHubCLIStatus.tooOld` + actionable copy

gh < 2.57 rejects `--json`, so a signed-in user currently reads as permanently logged out. Detect it
and say so:

- `static func rejectedUnknownFlag(_ r: CommandResult) -> Bool` — non-zero exit, no parseable JSON,
  stderr contains **`unknown flag`** matched *generically*, not the `--json` literal: `--active` has
  the same floor and gh reports whichever flag it parses first.
- New case in the classifier, ahead of the final fallback: `.verdict(.tooOld)`.
- Extract the panel copy out of the view body into a pure function and switch on all four states:

```swift
static func ghWarningCopy(for status: GitHubCLIStatus)
  -> (title: String, body: String, showsInstallLink: Bool)
```

`.tooOld` → "GitHub CLI too old" / "Workroom needs gh 2.57 or newer — run `brew upgrade gh`." and
**no** install link. `PullRequestPanel.swift:36`, `:42-44`, `:48` stop being ternaries.
`ChangesPanel.swift:220`/`:240` already gate on `== .available`, so they need no edit.

Rejected: re-running plain `gh auth status`. Two classifiers to keep in sync — the drift risk the
code warns about at `:485-488` — and it reinstates the #86 network-blip flap.

## 7. `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — instance-owned single-flight

Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, `AppStore` is
per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, and two windows both
probe with last-write-wins. Fix it with an **instance**, not a static — `AppStore.swift:793-795`
already guarantees tests get a fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs parallel, so static
state would let one test's fake runner serve another's probe while `reset()` cannot stop an in-flight
task repopulating the cache.

```
  GitHubAuthCache  (one per ProjectStore — isolation comes free)

   caller(force: false) ─┐
   caller(force: false) ─┼─► fresh within TTL? ──yes──► return cached verdict
   caller(force: false) ─┘            │no
                                      ▼
                          in-flight non-forced probe? ──yes──► JOIN it
                                      │no
                                      ▼
                        ┌── cache-owned Task { resolver.resolveGitHubCLI() }
                        │   (NOT the caller's task: a cancelled waiter no
                        │    longer SIGKILLs the gh child, so this path stops
                        │    producing killed results at all)
                        ▼
              .verdict(x) ─► store x + stamp monotonic instant
              .keepPrior  ─► keep previous verdict, DO NOT stamp

   caller(force: true) ──► never joins a non-forced flight; starts a NEW probe
                           (concurrent forced callers join each other)
```

Contracts, each written down and each tested:
- **Ownership.** The cache is the *sole* TTL owner. `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` and its
  `AppStore` proxy (`:296-299`) are **deleted**; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` remains as the
  SwiftUI-observable mirror.
- **Cancellation.** The probe runs in a cache-owned task, so it survives a cancelled waiter and
  yields a real verdict. The `Task.isCancelled` guard and `signaled` still earn their keep — OS
  kills, crashes, sleep/wake signals, and every other `CommandResult` consumer.
- **Force.** `force: true` starts a new probe rather than joining a non-forced flight, so Refresh
  really refreshes.
- **Clock.** Staleness is measured on a **monotonic** clock (`ContinuousClock`), not `Date`, so a
  backward wall-clock adjustment cannot extend the cache indefinitely. TTLs are init parameters, so
  the negative-TTL test runs in 50ms instead of sleeping. (The local/CI lanes keep their `Date`
  stamps; only this cache changes.)

## 8. Asymmetric TTL — 60s normal, 10s for `.notAuthenticated`

`.notAuthenticated` is both the alarming answer and the sink every ambiguous result used to fall
into, and it gates the entire PR/CI lane, so it is re-confirmed quickly. A genuine logout still warns
on the **first** probe; only caching shortens. Implement as an init parameter so the value is a
one-line tuning change — and **re-judge 10s once `.keepPrior` is in**, since not stamping an
ambiguous probe removes most of what this was compensating for. Flat rather than exponential matches
`applyCIStatus:567-568`, which already records backoff as a future refinement.

## 9. `UITestFixture.ghStatus` seam

Adding a flag alone changes nothing: `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode at `:104`. The
seeded status must be applied during fixture load **and** on manual reseeding, and must not be
overwritten by the optimistic `.available` default (`ProjectStore.swift:35`). That gap is why no
XCUITest can drive any gh state today.

---

# Lane C — independent, parallel with PR1

## 10. `VCSToolVersionCache` must not cache a `.notInstalled`

`ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:285-287`) silently returns the floor until the interactive-shell probe
lands, and the probe is fired detached at `WorkroomApp.swift:43` with nothing joining it while
`refreshVCSToolReport` runs from `apply(projects)` (`AppStore.swift:2492`). The floor covers
Homebrew but not a version-manager shim dir, Nix, or MacPorts — so a PATH miss gives 127, `status:149`
maps it to `.notInstalled`, `warnings:111-112` shows "jj isn't installed", and the cache pins it for
the whole process (`cached` is cleared only by the tests-only `reset()`).

Fix: cache only `.ok`, `.belowFloor`, and `.unknown`. A `.notInstalled` verdict re-probes on the next
call, against the by-then-enriched PATH. Fails in the safe direction — at worst a redundant
`--version`. (`.unknown` already fails safe: `warnings:107-108` ignores it.)

# Fix the false, sticky "GitHub CLI not signed in" in the PR panel

## Context

The PR panel intermittently claims `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then recovers on its own about a
minute later. Root cause confirmed by measurement.

A superseded status sweep (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:60`) or a workroom switched mid-probe
(`:118`) cancels the task awaiting `gh auth status --active --json hosts`. The runner's `onCancel`
SIGKILLs the child (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:301-307`), but its `withCheckedContinuation` is
**non-throwing**, so `terminationHandler` (`:252-268`) still resumes with `exitCode: 9` (SIGKILL —
measured; signal numbers stay well below `commandNotFound: 127`), `timedOut: false`, and
empty-or-half-written stdout.

That walks the classifier (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:434-444`): not 127, not timed out, no
parseable JSON, so it falls to `r.ok ? .available : .notAuthenticated` → **`.notAuthenticated`**.

`refreshGitHubCLI` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:103-113`) then writes that verdict **and stamps
`ghStatusCheckedAt`** with no `Task.isCancelled` check. It is the only mutation in that file buried
*behind* an await, so the callers' guards at `:86`/`:144` come too late. The stamp is the sticky
half: the TTL gate at `:105-109` early-returns for every unforced caller, so for 60s every lane that
would have healed the value is suppressed by the value's own stamp, while `:87`/`:145` gate off the
whole CI/PR probe. Only the manual Refresh button (`ChangesPanel.swift:143`, the sole `force: true`
path) escapes early. The verdict lives on the process-wide `ProjectStore.shared.githubCLIStatus`, so
one window's cancelled probe paints and suppresses every other window's panel.

```
  THE POISONED-CACHE LOOP  (what makes a 200ms blip last 60 seconds)

  lane B starts ──cancel()──► lane A's `gh auth status` child
                                      │ SIGKILL
                                      ▼
                        CommandResult(exitCode: 9, timedOut: false, stdout: "")
                                      │
                     classifyGitHubCLI │ not 127 · not timedOut · no JSON
                                      ▼
                             .notAuthenticated          ◄── a lie: nothing was learned
                                      │
                  refreshGitHubCLI:112 │ writes value AND stamps TTL   (no isCancelled guard)
                                      ▼
                 ProjectStore.shared ──┬──► PR panel: "GitHub CLI not signed in"   (every window)
                                       └──► ghStatusCheckedAt = now
                                                     │
                     ┌───────────────────────────────┘
                     ▼
              TTL gate :105-109 ──► every unforced caller returns EARLY for 60s
                     │                    ▲
                     └────────────────────┘  the wrong value suppresses its own repair
                          escape hatch: ONLY the Refresh button (force: true)
```

Measured against real gh 2.97.0: the `--json` payload goes to **stdout** and exit is **0** in all
three genuine states (signed in `state:"success"`; bad token `state:"error"` + `HTTP 401 ... Bad
credentials`; no config `{"hosts":{}}`). So the exit-code fallback is never reached in normal
operation — everything landing there is ambiguous by construction. A keyring/transport failure
produces a *populated* host entry with a non-401 error, already routed away by
`isGitHubAuthFailure` (`:479-482`).

Outcome wanted: an uninformative probe must never publish anything, and an ambiguous one must never
be trusted for a minute.

## What already exists (reuse, don't rebuild)

| Sub-problem | Existing code | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| "child died by signal; exit code is a signal number" | `WorkroomCLI.swift:35-44` `CLIResult.signaled`, consumed `:287`; shipped as `a64e4269` "stop 'exited with code 15' dialog on wake from sleep" | Copy the field and the name onto `CommandResult` |
| "a blip must not overwrite a good value" | `ghPreflight` `.keepPrior` (`:489-504`); `applyCIStatus:564-570` / `applyPRStatus:596-599` don't-stamp-on-first-blip | Adopt `.keepPrior` for the auth probe too |
| cancellation guard idiom | `Task.isCancelled` at `:82`, `:86`, `:96`, `:136`, `:140`, `:144`, `:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`, `:446`, `:493`, `:724` | Same idiom, moved inside `refreshGitHubCLI` |
| "machine fact, one probe for N windows" | `VCSToolVersionCache` actor (`VCSToolVersions.swift:183-206`) — the pattern, but **static**, which is why we deviate | Instance-owned, see PR2 |
| tool floor + warn, don't guess | git ≥ 2.41 / jj ≥ 0.43 floors, `warnings(hasJJProject:)` | `.tooOld` follows the same posture for gh |
| test isolation | `AppStore.swift:793-795` — "tests build an isolated `AppStore()` (own fresh `ProjectStore`)" | Own the cache per `ProjectStore` so this holds for free |
| signalled-probe safety, already correct | `VCSToolVersions.status:148-154` maps a signalled `--version` to `.unknown`, which `warnings:107-108` ignores | No change; verified not affected |

Nothing here is rebuilt. The one genuinely new type is `GitHubAuthCache` (PR2).

---

# PR1 — the fix (small, independently revertable)

## 1. `CommandResult.signaled` — `Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`

- `CommandResult` (`:8-20`) gains `let signaled: Bool` plus an **explicit init** with
  `signaled: Bool = false` last. Do **not** write `let signaled: Bool = false`: Swift drops a
  `let` with an initial value from the synthesized memberwise init entirely, and the only compile
  error is the one line that tries to set it. All ~63 `CommandResult(` sites use labelled args, so a
  trailing defaulted parameter keeps every one compiling; no consumer compares whole values, so the
  widened synthesized `==` breaks nothing.
- `terminationHandler` (`:262-267`): `signaled: finished.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal`.
- **Trap to comment loudly:** the timeout path calls `proc.terminate()` (`:239`) — SIGTERM — so a
  timed-out child has `timedOut == true` **AND** `signaled == true`. Every consumer must therefore
  test `timedOut` first. `markTimedOut()` already precedes `terminate()` at `:237-240`, so the
  ordering is safe as long as classifiers respect it.

## 2. "No news" becomes representable — `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`

`.available` is not "no news", it is a positive claim that gh works — and writing it over a correct
`.notAuthenticated` erases a true warning with a false silence. The codebase already has the right
word two functions down (`ghPreflight`'s `.keepPrior`). So:

```swift
enum GHAuthProbe: Equatable {
  case verdict(GitHubCLIStatus)
  case keepPrior          // the probe told us nothing — killed, crashed, timed out
}

static func classifyGitHubCLI(_ r: CommandResult) -> GHAuthProbe {
  if r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .verdict(.notInstalled) }
  if r.timedOut { return .keepPrior }                                  // MUST precede signaled
  if let s = classifyGitHubCLIJSON(r.stdout) { return .verdict(s) }     // a complete verdict wins
  if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }                                  // no verdict ⇒ no evidence
  return r.ok ? .verdict(.available) : .verdict(.notAuthenticated)
}
```

`resolveGitHubCLI()` returns `GHAuthProbe`. Two orderings are load-bearing and both get a test:
`timedOut` before `signaled` (a timeout is also a signal), and the JSON parse before `signaled` (a
child that emitted a complete 401 and was *then* killed has genuinely told us the token is bad).

This also corrects the pre-existing `.available`-on-timeout lie at `:436`.

`ghPreflight` (`:495-504`) gets `if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }` immediately after its own
`timedOut` check. Not a live bug — all four apply sites (`:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`) are guarded
— so comment it as braces to those guards' belt.

## 3. Nothing from a cancelled or uninformative probe is published — `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`

```swift
let probe = await resolver.resolveGitHubCLI()
if Task.isCancelled { return }                            // a cancelled probe holds no fact
guard case .verdict(let status) = probe else { return }   // .keepPrior: no write, NO STAMP
githubCLIStatus = status
ghStatusCheckedAt = Date()
```

Bail entirely rather than write-value-but-skip-stamp: a cancelled probe's value is garbage too.
Comment why, because the instinct that produced the bug ("a machine-global fact is worth recording
even from a cancelled task") is defensible and wrong.

`.keepPrior` deliberately does **not** stamp, so the next lane re-probes instead of trusting a
non-answer for the full TTL. That is the structural repair; the asymmetric TTL in PR2 is then only
about re-confirming a *real* `.notAuthenticated` sooner.

## 4. `VCSWriting.swift` — stop printing a signal number as an exit code

`:1099` and `:1197` end with `.other("\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)")` when stderr is empty, so a
signalled `git push` renders the literal `git exited 15` in the failure sheet — verbatim the dialog
`a64e4269` claims to have stopped, because that fix never reached this runner. Insert immediately
before each fallback, so any real stderr still classifies:

```swift
let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other("\(tool) was interrupted") }
return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
```

`.other` already carries Retry as its recovery, which is correct for an interrupted write, so no new
enum case. **Rebase note:** `VCSWriting.swift` has uncommitted changes in the working tree.

## 5. Prose corrections (part of the change, not follow-ups)

- `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:440-442` claims the fallback covers "pre-2.57 gh without `--json`".
  Measured false — an old gh *rejects* the flag (exit 1, empty stdout, `unknown flag: --json`).
  Rewrite to say what the fallback actually covers, and point at PR2 for the real handling.
- `TODOS.md:202-207` defers the `withTimeout` cancellation fix on the grounds that "every call site
  already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result … so state stays correct". This bug
  is the counterexample, and the consequence was a wrong published value, not wasted CPU. Correct the
  rationale; **keep the deferral** — that entry's mechanism (`withTimeout`) is genuinely unrelated to
  this one (`runner.run`'s non-throwing continuation).

---

# PR2 — hardening (all approved, lands after PR1)

## 6. `GitHubCLIStatus.tooOld` + actionable copy

gh < 2.57 rejects `--json`, so a signed-in user currently reads as permanently logged out. Detect it
and say so:

- `static func rejectedUnknownFlag(_ r: CommandResult) -> Bool` — non-zero exit, no parseable JSON,
  stderr contains **`unknown flag`** matched *generically*, not the `--json` literal: `--active` has
  the same floor and gh reports whichever flag it parses first.

## 7. `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — instance-owned single-flight

Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, `AppStore` is
per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, and two windows both
probe with last-write-wins. Fix it with an **instance**, not a static — `AppStore.swift:793-795`
already guarantees tests get a fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs parallel, so static
state would let one test's fake runner serve another's probe while `reset()` cannot stop an in-flight
task repopulating the cache.

```
  GitHubAuthCache  (one per ProjectStore — isolation comes free)

   caller(force: false) ─┐
   caller(force: false) ─┼─► fresh within TTL? ──yes──► return cached verdict
   caller(force: false) ─┘            │no
                                      ▼
                          in-flight non-forced probe? ──yes──► JOIN it
                                      │no
                                      ▼
                        ┌── cache-owned Task { resolver.resolveGitHubCLI() }
                        │   (NOT the caller's task: a cancelled waiter no
                        │    longer SIGKILLs the gh child, so this path stops
                        │    producing killed results at all)
                        ▼
              .verdict(x) ─► store x + stamp monotonic instant
              .keepPrior  ─► keep previous verdict, DO NOT stamp

   caller(force: true) ──► never joins a non-forced flight; starts a NEW probe
                           (concurrent forced callers join each other)
```

Contracts, each written down and each tested:
- **Ownership.** The cache is the *sole* TTL owner. `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` and its
  `AppStore` proxy (`:296-299`) are **deleted**; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` remains as the
  SwiftUI-observable mirror.
- **Cancellation.** The probe runs in a cache-owned task, so it survives a cancelled waiter and
  yields a real verdict. The `Task.isCancelled` guard and `signaled` still earn their keep — OS
  kills, crashes, sleep/wake signals, and every other `CommandResult` consumer.
- **Force.** `force: true` starts a new probe rather than joining a non-forced flight, so Refresh
  really refreshes.
- **Clock.** Staleness is measured on a **monotonic** clock (`ContinuousClock`), not `Date`, so a
  backward wall-clock adjustment cannot extend the cache indefinitely. TTLs are init parameters, so
  the negative-TTL test runs in 50ms instead of sleeping. (The local/CI lanes keep their `Date`
  stamps; only this cache changes.)

## 8. Asymmetric TTL — 60s normal, 10s for `.notAuthenticated`

`.notAuthenticated` is both the alarming answer and the sink every ambiguous result used to fall
into, and it gates the entire PR/CI lane, so it is re-confirmed quickly. A genuine logout still warns
on the **first** probe; only caching shortens. Implement as an init parameter so the value is a
one-line tuning change — and **re-judge 10s once `.keepPrior` is in**, since not stamping an
ambiguous probe removes most of what this was compensating for. Flat rather than exponential matches
`applyCIStatus:567-568`, which already records backoff as a future refinement.

## 9. `UITestFixture.ghStatus` seam

Adding a flag alone changes nothing: `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode at `:104`. The
seeded status must be applied during fixture load **and** on manual reseeding, and must not be
overwritten by the optimistic `.available` default (`ProjectStore.swift:35`). That gap is why no
XCUITest can drive any gh state today.

## 10. `VCSToolVersionCache` must not cache a `.notInstalled`

`ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:285-287`) silently returns the floor until the interactive-shell probe
lands, and the probe is fired detached at `WorkroomApp.swift:43` with nothing joining it while
`refreshVCSToolReport` runs from `apply(projects)` (`AppStore.swift:2492`). The floor covers
Homebrew but not a version-manager shim dir, Nix, or MacPorts — so a PATH miss gives 127, `status:149`
maps it to `.notInstalled`, `warnings:111-112` shows "jj isn't installed", and the cache pins it for
the whole process (`cached` is cleared only by the tests-only `reset()`).

Fix: cache only `.ok`, `.belowFloor`, and `.unknown`. A `.notInstalled` verdict re-probes on the next
call, against the by-then-enriched PATH. Fails in the safe direction — at worst a redundant
`--version`. (`.unknown` already fails safe: `warnings:107-108` ignores it.)

+## 7. `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — instance-owned single-flight
+Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, `AppStore` is
+per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, and two windows both
+probe with last-write-wins. Fix it with an **instance**, not a static — `AppStore.swift:793-795`
+already guarantees tests get a fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs parallel, so static
+state would let one test's fake runner serve another's probe while `reset()` cannot stop an in-flight
+task repopulating the cache.
+  GitHubAuthCache  (one per ProjectStore — isolation comes free)
+   caller(force: false) ─┐
+   caller(force: false) ─┼─► fresh within TTL? ──yes──► return cached verdict
+   caller(force: false) ─┘            │no
+                          in-flight non-forced probe? ──yes──► JOIN it
+                                      │no
+                        ┌── cache-owned Task { resolver.resolveGitHubCLI() }
+                        │   (NOT the caller's task: a cancelled waiter no
+                        │    longer SIGKILLs the gh child, so this path stops
+                        │    producing killed results at all)
+              .verdict(x) ─► store x + stamp monotonic instant
+              .keepPrior  ─► keep previous verdict, DO NOT stamp
+   caller(force: true) ──► never joins a non-forced flight; starts a NEW probe
+                           (concurrent forced callers join each other)
+Contracts, each written down and each tested:
+- **Ownership.** The cache is the *sole* TTL owner. `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` and its
+  `AppStore` proxy (`:296-299`) are **deleted**; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` remains as the
+  SwiftUI-observable mirror.
+- **Cancellation.** The probe runs in a cache-owned task, so it survives a cancelled waiter and
+  yields a real verdict. The `Task.isCancelled` guard and `signaled` still earn their keep — OS
+  kills, crashes, sleep/wake signals, and every other `CommandResult` consumer.
+- **Force.** `force: true` starts a new probe rather than joining a non-forced flight, so Refresh
+  really refreshes.

# Fix the false, sticky "GitHub CLI not signed in" in the PR panel

## Context

The PR panel intermittently claims `GitHub CLI not signed in`, then recovers on its own about a
minute later. Root cause confirmed by measurement.

A superseded status sweep (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:60`) or a workroom switched mid-probe
(`:118`) cancels the task awaiting `gh auth status --active --json hosts`. The runner's `onCancel`
SIGKILLs the child (`StatusCommandRunner.swift:301-307`), but its `withCheckedContinuation` is
**non-throwing**, so `terminationHandler` (`:252-268`) still resumes with `exitCode: 9` (SIGKILL —
measured; signal numbers stay well below `commandNotFound: 127`), `timedOut: false`, and
empty-or-half-written stdout.

That walks the classifier (`WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:434-444`): not 127, not timed out, no
parseable JSON, so it falls to `r.ok ? .available : .notAuthenticated` → **`.notAuthenticated`**.

`refreshGitHubCLI` (`AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift:103-113`) then writes that verdict **and stamps
`ghStatusCheckedAt`** with no `Task.isCancelled` check. It is the only mutation in that file buried
*behind* an await, so the callers' guards at `:86`/`:144` come too late. The stamp is the sticky
half: the TTL gate at `:105-109` early-returns for every unforced caller, so for 60s every lane that
would have healed the value is suppressed by the value's own stamp, while `:87`/`:145` gate off the
whole CI/PR probe. Only the manual Refresh button (`ChangesPanel.swift:143`, the sole `force: true`
path) escapes early. The verdict lives on the process-wide `ProjectStore.shared.githubCLIStatus`, so
one window's cancelled probe paints and suppresses every other window's panel.

```
  THE POISONED-CACHE LOOP  (what makes a 200ms blip last 60 seconds)

  lane B starts ──cancel()──► lane A's `gh auth status` child
                                      │ SIGKILL
                                      ▼
                        CommandResult(exitCode: 9, timedOut: false, stdout: "")
                                      │
                     classifyGitHubCLI │ not 127 · not timedOut · no JSON
                                      ▼
                             .notAuthenticated          ◄── a lie: nothing was learned
                                      │
                  refreshGitHubCLI:112 │ writes value AND stamps TTL   (no isCancelled guard)
                                      ▼
                 ProjectStore.shared ──┬──► PR panel: "GitHub CLI not signed in"   (every window)
                                       └──► ghStatusCheckedAt = now
                                                     │
                     ┌───────────────────────────────┘
                     ▼
              TTL gate :105-109 ──► every unforced caller returns EARLY for 60s
                     │                    ▲
                     └────────────────────┘  the wrong value suppresses its own repair
                          escape hatch: ONLY the Refresh button (force: true)
```

Measured against real gh 2.97.0: the `--json` payload goes to **stdout** and exit is **0** in all
three genuine states (signed in `state:"success"`; bad token `state:"error"` + `HTTP 401 ... Bad
credentials`; no config `{"hosts":{}}`). So the exit-code fallback is never reached in normal
operation — everything landing there is ambiguous by construction. A keyring/transport failure
produces a *populated* host entry with a non-401 error, already routed away by
`isGitHubAuthFailure` (`:479-482`).

Outcome wanted: an uninformative probe must never publish anything, and an ambiguous one must never
be trusted for a minute.

## What already exists (reuse, don't rebuild)

| Sub-problem | Existing code | Plan |
|---|---|---|
| "child died by signal; exit code is a signal number" | `WorkroomCLI.swift:35-44` `CLIResult.signaled`, consumed `:287`; shipped as `a64e4269` "stop 'exited with code 15' dialog on wake from sleep" | Copy the field and the name onto `CommandResult` |
| "a blip must not overwrite a good value" | `ghPreflight` `.keepPrior` (`:489-504`); `applyCIStatus:564-570` / `applyPRStatus:596-599` don't-stamp-on-first-blip | Adopt `.keepPrior` for the auth probe too |
| cancellation guard idiom | `Task.isCancelled` at `:82`, `:86`, `:96`, `:136`, `:140`, `:144`, `:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`, `:446`, `:493`, `:724` | Same idiom, moved inside `refreshGitHubCLI` |
| "machine fact, one probe for N windows" | `VCSToolVersionCache` actor (`VCSToolVersions.swift:183-206`) — the pattern, but **static**, which is why we deviate | Instance-owned, see PR2 |
| tool floor + warn, don't guess | git ≥ 2.41 / jj ≥ 0.43 floors, `warnings(hasJJProject:)` | `.tooOld` follows the same posture for gh |
| test isolation | `AppStore.swift:793-795` — "tests build an isolated `AppStore()` (own fresh `ProjectStore`)" | Own the cache per `ProjectStore` so this holds for free |
| signalled-probe safety, already correct | `VCSToolVersions.status:148-154` maps a signalled `--version` to `.unknown`, which `warnings:107-108` ignores | No change; verified not affected |

Nothing here is rebuilt. The one genuinely new type is `GitHubAuthCache` (PR2).

---

# PR1 — the fix (small, independently revertable)

## 1. `CommandResult.signaled` — `Core/StatusCommandRunner.swift`

- `CommandResult` (`:8-20`) gains `let signaled: Bool` plus an **explicit init** with
  `signaled: Bool = false` last. Do **not** write `let signaled: Bool = false`: Swift drops a
  `let` with an initial value from the synthesized memberwise init entirely, and the only compile
  error is the one line that tries to set it. All ~63 `CommandResult(` sites use labelled args, so a
  trailing defaulted parameter keeps every one compiling; no consumer compares whole values, so the
  widened synthesized `==` breaks nothing.
- `terminationHandler` (`:262-267`): `signaled: finished.terminationReason == .uncaughtSignal`.
- **Trap to comment loudly:** the timeout path calls `proc.terminate()` (`:239`) — SIGTERM — so a
  timed-out child has `timedOut == true` **AND** `signaled == true`. Every consumer must therefore
  test `timedOut` first. `markTimedOut()` already precedes `terminate()` at `:237-240`, so the
  ordering is safe as long as classifiers respect it.

## 2. "No news" becomes representable — `Core/WorkroomStatusResolver.swift`

`.available` is not "no news", it is a positive claim that gh works — and writing it over a correct
`.notAuthenticated` erases a true warning with a false silence. The codebase already has the right
word two functions down (`ghPreflight`'s `.keepPrior`). So:

```swift
enum GHAuthProbe: Equatable {
  case verdict(GitHubCLIStatus)
  case keepPrior          // the probe told us nothing — killed, crashed, timed out
}

static func classifyGitHubCLI(_ r: CommandResult) -> GHAuthProbe {
  if r.exitCode == CommandResult.commandNotFound { return .verdict(.notInstalled) }
  if r.timedOut { return .keepPrior }                                  // MUST precede signaled
  if let s = classifyGitHubCLIJSON(r.stdout) { return .verdict(s) }     // a complete verdict wins
  if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }                                  // no verdict ⇒ no evidence
  return r.ok ? .verdict(.available) : .verdict(.notAuthenticated)
}
```

`resolveGitHubCLI()` returns `GHAuthProbe`. Two orderings are load-bearing and both get a test:
`timedOut` before `signaled` (a timeout is also a signal), and the JSON parse before `signaled` (a
child that emitted a complete 401 and was *then* killed has genuinely told us the token is bad).

This also corrects the pre-existing `.available`-on-timeout lie at `:436`.

`ghPreflight` (`:495-504`) gets `if r.signaled { return .keepPrior }` immediately after its own
`timedOut` check. Not a live bug — all four apply sites (`:153`, `:156`, `:166`, `:169`) are guarded
— so comment it as braces to those guards' belt.

## 3. Nothing from a cancelled or uninformative probe is published — `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift`

```swift
let probe = await resolver.resolveGitHubCLI()
if Task.isCancelled { return }                            // a cancelled probe holds no fact
guard case .verdict(let status) = probe else { return }   // .keepPrior: no write, NO STAMP
githubCLIStatus = status
ghStatusCheckedAt = Date()
```

Bail entirely rather than write-value-but-skip-stamp: a cancelled probe's value is garbage too.
Comment why, because the instinct that produced the bug ("a machine-global fact is worth recording
even from a cancelled task") is defensible and wrong.

`.keepPrior` deliberately does **not** stamp, so the next lane re-probes instead of trusting a
non-answer for the full TTL. That is the structural repair; the asymmetric TTL in PR2 is then only
about re-confirming a *real* `.notAuthenticated` sooner.

## 4. `VCSWriting.swift` — stop printing a signal number as an exit code

`:1099` and `:1197` end with `.other("\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)")` when stderr is empty, so a
signalled `git push` renders the literal `git exited 15` in the failure sheet — verbatim the dialog
`a64e4269` claims to have stopped, because that fix never reached this runner. Insert immediately
before each fallback, so any real stderr still classifies:

```swift
let trimmed = err.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
if trimmed.isEmpty, result.signaled { return .other("\(tool) was interrupted") }
return .other(trimmed.isEmpty ? "\(tool) exited \(result.exitCode)" : trimmed)
```

`.other` already carries Retry as its recovery, which is correct for an interrupted write, so no new
enum case. **Rebase note:** `VCSWriting.swift` has uncommitted changes in the working tree.

## 5. Prose corrections (part of the change, not follow-ups)

- `WorkroomStatusResolver.swift:440-442` claims the fallback covers "pre-2.57 gh without `--json`".
  Measured false — an old gh *rejects* the flag (exit 1, empty stdout, `unknown flag: --json`).
  Rewrite to say what the fallback actually covers, and point at PR2 for the real handling.
- `TODOS.md:202-207` defers the `withTimeout` cancellation fix on the grounds that "every call site
  already checks `Task.isCancelled` before merging a stale result … so state stays correct". This bug
  is the counterexample, and the consequence was a wrong published value, not wasted CPU. Correct the
  rationale; **keep the deferral** — that entry's mechanism (`withTimeout`) is genuinely unrelated to
  this one (`runner.run`'s non-throwing continuation).

---

# PR2 — hardening (all approved, lands after PR1)

## 6. `GitHubCLIStatus.tooOld` + actionable copy

gh < 2.57 rejects `--json`, so a signed-in user currently reads as permanently logged out. Detect it
and say so:

- `static func rejectedUnknownFlag(_ r: CommandResult) -> Bool` — non-zero exit, no parseable JSON,
  stderr contains **`unknown flag`** matched *generically*, not the `--json` literal: `--active` has
  the same floor and gh reports whichever flag it parses first.
- New case in the classifier, ahead of the final fallback: `.verdict(.tooOld)`.
- Extract the panel copy out of the view body into a pure function and switch on all four states:

```swift
static func ghWarningCopy(for status: GitHubCLIStatus)
  -> (title: String, body: String, showsInstallLink: Bool)
```

`.tooOld` → "GitHub CLI too old" / "Workroom needs gh 2.57 or newer — run `brew upgrade gh`." and
**no** install link. `PullRequestPanel.swift:36`, `:42-44`, `:48` stop being ternaries.
`ChangesPanel.swift:220`/`:240` already gate on `== .available`, so they need no edit.

Rejected: re-running plain `gh auth status`. Two classifiers to keep in sync — the drift risk the
code warns about at `:485-488` — and it reinstates the #86 network-blip flap.

## 7. `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — instance-owned single-flight

Today the TTL read (`:105-109`) sits before the await and the stamp (`:112`) after it, `AppStore` is
per-window (`WorkroomApp.swift:103`) while the verdict is a shared singleton, and two windows both
probe with last-write-wins. Fix it with an **instance**, not a static — `AppStore.swift:793-795`
already guarantees tests get a fresh `ProjectStore`, and `make app-test` runs parallel, so static
state would let one test's fake runner serve another's probe while `reset()` cannot stop an in-flight
task repopulating the cache.

```
  GitHubAuthCache  (one per ProjectStore — isolation comes free)

   caller(force: false) ─┐
   caller(force: false) ─┼─► fresh within TTL? ──yes──► return cached verdict
   caller(force: false) ─┘            │no
                                      ▼
                          in-flight non-forced probe? ──yes──► JOIN it
                                      │no
                                      ▼
                        ┌── cache-owned Task { resolver.resolveGitHubCLI() }
                        │   (NOT the caller's task: a cancelled waiter no
                        │    longer SIGKILLs the gh child, so this path stops
                        │    producing killed results at all)
                        ▼
              .verdict(x) ─► store x + stamp monotonic instant
              .keepPrior  ─► keep previous verdict, DO NOT stamp

   caller(force: true) ──► never joins a non-forced flight; starts a NEW probe
                           (concurrent forced callers join each other)
```

Contracts, each written down and each tested:
- **Ownership.** The cache is the *sole* TTL owner. `ProjectStore.ghStatusCheckedAt` and its
  `AppStore` proxy (`:296-299`) are **deleted**; `ProjectStore.githubCLIStatus` remains as the
  SwiftUI-observable mirror.
- **Cancellation.** The probe runs in a cache-owned task, so it survives a cancelled waiter and
  yields a real verdict. The `Task.isCancelled` guard and `signaled` still earn their keep — OS
  kills, crashes, sleep/wake signals, and every other `CommandResult` consumer.
- **Force.** `force: true` starts a new probe rather than joining a non-forced flight, so Refresh
  really refreshes.
- **Clock.** Staleness is measured on a **monotonic** clock (`ContinuousClock`), not `Date`, so a
  backward wall-clock adjustment cannot extend the cache indefinitely. TTLs are init parameters, so
  the negative-TTL test runs in 50ms instead of sleeping. (The local/CI lanes keep their `Date`
  stamps; only this cache changes.)

## 8. Asymmetric TTL — 60s normal, 10s for `.notAuthenticated`

`.notAuthenticated` is both the alarming answer and the sink every ambiguous result used to fall
into, and it gates the entire PR/CI lane, so it is re-confirmed quickly. A genuine logout still warns
on the **first** probe; only caching shortens. Implement as an init parameter so the value is a
one-line tuning change — and **re-judge 10s once `.keepPrior` is in**, since not stamping an
ambiguous probe removes most of what this was compensating for. Flat rather than exponential matches
`applyCIStatus:567-568`, which already records backoff as a future refinement.

## 9. `UITestFixture.ghStatus` seam

Adding a flag alone changes nothing: `refreshGitHubCLI` hard-returns in fixture mode at `:104`. The
seeded status must be applied during fixture load **and** on manual reseeding, and must not be
overwritten by the optimistic `.available` default (`ProjectStore.swift:35`). That gap is why no
XCUITest can drive any gh state today.

---

# Lane C — independent, parallel with PR1

## 10. `VCSToolVersionCache` must not cache a `.notInstalled`

`ShellEnvironment.path()` (`:285-287`) silently returns the floor until the interactive-shell probe
lands, and the probe is fired detached at `WorkroomApp.swift:43` with nothing joining it while
`refreshVCSToolReport` runs from `apply(projects)` (`AppStore.swift:2492`). The floor covers
Homebrew but not a version-manager shim dir, Nix, or MacPorts — so a PATH miss gives 127, `status:149`
maps it to `.notInstalled`, `warnings:111-112` shows "jj isn't installed", and the cache pins it for
the whole process (`cached` is cleared only by the tests-only `reset()`).

Fix: cache only `.ok`, `.belowFloor`, and `.unknown`. A `.notInstalled` verdict re-probes on the next
call, against the by-then-enriched PATH. Fails in the safe direction — at worst a redundant
`--version`. (`.unknown` already fails safe: `warnings:107-108` ignores it.)

---

## Inline ASCII diagrams to add in code

Per the diagram-maintenance rule, these go in the same commits:

- `WorkroomStatusResolver.classifyGitHubCLI` — the decision tree, with the two load-bearing
  orderings marked (`timedOut` before `signaled`; JSON parse before `signaled`).
- `AppStore+WorkroomStatus.swift` header — the two lanes, who cancels whom, and the rule that no
  result may be published after the await without a cancellation check.
- `Core/GitHubAuthCache.swift` — the single-flight / force / TTL lifecycle diagram above.
- `StatusCommandRunner.CommandResult` — a one-line note that `timedOut` implies `signaled`.

## Tests
